product:
Undirect is a Safari web extension for Mac, iPhone and iPad, with a small
companion app. It stops the tricks pages use to take a click that was not meant
for them: an invisible layer laid over the page, a link whose destination
changes between the press and the release, a pop-up window or new tab opened to
somewhere else, and a same-tab redirect fired the moment a press lands. The
guard only watches sites the person has switched it on for, one at a time, from
the Undirect button in Safari's toolbar. Every outside destination a watched
page reaches for becomes a row the person can allow or block, for that one site
or for every site. The Mac app lets them review and edit those rows; the
iPhone/iPad app can only show them and turn a site's watching off, because iOS
gives a container app no way to message its own extension. The audience is
ordinary Safari users protecting their own browsing, not IT admins, so the tone
throughout is plain, calm and matter-of-fact: it reports what happened and what
the person can do next, never alarms them or explains how the trick works
technically.

vocabulary.meaning: the extension's protection itself, as a thing that can be on or off (master switch), and as the ongoing act of watching a page
a website the person has individually switched the guard on for, from the Undirect toolbar button; the guard only runs there (unless the 'every site' mode is chosen)
the other website a link, window or redirect was trying to send the person to; identified by its base domain, not the full URL
a stored decision (allow or block) for one destination, scoped either to a single site or to every site; a destination with no rule falls back to the default policy
whether a rule applies only on the current site ('here') or on every guarded site ('everywhere'); a rule set for one site wins over one set everywhere, which wins over the default
the two verdicts a rule (or the default policy) can hold for a destination: block stops it, allow lets it through
what happens to a destination that has no rule at all yet; a global setting, itself either 'block' or 'allow'
the user's own tap or click; the guard's job is making sure a press only ever does what the person aimed it at, never something a page substituted afterward
'site' is the whole domain the guard is switched on or off for; 'page' is the one tab currently open, whose specific attempts are listed separately from the site-wide rule list
one instance of a page trying to hijack a press (of any kind - overlay, swapped link, popup, redirect); 'stopped' counts how many were blocked, distinct from how many were merely seen
which specific trick was used for one attempt - e.g. an invisible click-catcher, a link swapped mid-press, a pop-up window, a redirect - shown as a short label per row

vocabulary.concept: note in the page / page note
vocabulary.meaning: an optional small on-page banner the guard can draw when it stops something, separate from the popup; off by default
the extension background page's own lifetime in memory; on iOS it can be unloaded at any time, so anything that must survive is written to disk rather than kept only in memory
the Undirect icon in Safari's toolbar; pressing it on an off site turns guarding on for that site (and reloads it); its icon and tooltip reflect on/off/no-site state
